original_test_intent: Prove that persistence mode can be enabled and disabled on every intended NVIDIA GPU and that each requested state is observable, with the original configuration restored.
original_method: Identify GPU UUID/BDF scope and baseline persistence state; drain/confirm no sensitive clients; obtain approval; execute enable and verify per device, then disable and verify; preserve exits/errors/timestamps; restore each GPU to its individual baseline even if the test fails and confirm health.
manual_activity: Operator approves driver-state mutation and workload isolation; after approval the agent may execute both transitions, verify them and restore each baseline.
required_inputs: GPU UUID/BDF scope and per-device original mode
safety_requirements: Never change mode with active unapproved GPU clients
Do not assume all baselines are Disabled
Restore every original state on all exit paths
No automatic retry, driver reload or GPU reset
agent_execution_scope: Validate approval, scope, baseline and quiescence
Execute one approved enable/verify and disable/verify sequence
Restore exact baselines and collect health

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its read-only query misses the source's required -pm 1 and -pm 0 transitions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approval, target the manifest GPU set explicitly, capture each baseline, perform enable/read then disable/read and finally restore individual baselines.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both source state transitions and both expected strings are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat persistence changes as a logged transaction with per-GPU baseline, two transition checkpoints and guaranteed restore.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity, isolation and rollback without weakening transition coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Unlike DeepSeek's inventory-only command, exercises both source-required states.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Changing persistence can affect driver lifecycle behavior and active contexts; service policy may reapply a state.

project_override_considerations: Project policy must define whether nvidia-persistenced manages the state and which GPUs may be changed during the window.
expected_evidence: Exact enable/read/disable/read commands, outputs, exits and timestamps
Baseline restore and final driver/GPU health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require both persistence-mode transitions; DeepSeek incompleteness is not a Master conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation is supportable once maintenance approval and restore inputs are provided.

review_improvement: Restores the state-changing coverage omitted by DeepSeek and makes it a reversible per-device transaction.
independent_technical_reasoning: Persistence mode is driver state, so reading its current value cannot prove enable and disable controls. Because the source deliberately exercises both directions, safe automation requires baseline capture, quiescence and finally-style restoration rather than treating the query as read-only validation.
